terms.gloss: the dishonour of illicit sex: seduction, fornication, rape, as a disgrace to the one dishonoured
evidence: Plaut. Amph. 883: stuprī, dēdecoris ā virō argūtam meō
Cic. Tusc. 4.75: stupra et corruptēlae et adulteria, incesta dēnique (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In the oldest Latin simply disgrace. Lewis & Short: it always implies dishonour done to the person, man or woman, and is not used of dealings with prostitutes; its opposite is pudīcitia. With force it is rape: stuprum per vim.

phrases.latin: ita mē probrī, stuprī, dēdecoris ā virō argūtam meō!
phrases.english: to think that my own husband should accuse me so of shame, of unchastity, of disgrace!
on this side chastity, on that debauchery

sources: Lewis & Short: stuprum · Lewis & Short: impudicitia
